safe_temperature.temperature: Cook until yolk & white are firm (FDA standard for whole eggs); 160°F for egg dishes and casseroles

source.name: SAFE MINIMUM INTERNAL TEMPERATURES as measured with a food thermometer - FDA

safe_temperature.disagreements: The FDA food safety standard mandates cooking eggs until both yolk and white are completely firm, and heating egg dishes to 160°F. However, culinary sources in the notebook (Food Network Kitchen's '10 Mistakes Everyone Makes Cooking Eggs') state that overcooking proteins forces out moisture and renders eggs tough and rubbery. For classic preparations like sunny-side up, soft-boiled, and over-easy, culinary doneness intentionally leaves the yolk runny (below 160°F) while ensuring the white is fully opaque and set.

avoid.warning: Adding eggs to a cold pan: Eggs cook unevenly as the pan warms up and proteins seep into pan pores before setting, causing stubborn sticking.

source.name: 10 Mistakes Everyone Makes Cooking Eggs - Food Network
source.location: Mistake 2: Adding Eggs to a Cold Pan

avoid.warning: Cooking over high heat: High temperatures force out water from proteins, resulting in rubbery, tough eggs with leathery whites before yolks can set.

source.name: 10 Mistakes Everyone Makes Cooking Eggs - Food Network
source.location: Mistake 4: Cooking Eggs Over High Heat

avoid.warning: Cracking eggs on the rim of a bowl: Rim cracking shatters the shell, driving shards and surface bacteria into the egg white. Always crack on a flat surface.

source.name: 10 Mistakes Everyone Makes Cooking Eggs - Food Network
source.location: Mistake 5: Cracking Eggs on the Edge of a Bowl

avoid.warning: Over-boiling hard-cooked eggs: Boiling too long produces an unappetizing sulfuric green-gray ring around the yolk.

source.name: 10 Mistakes Everyone Makes Cooking Eggs - Food Network

avoid.warning: Peeling eggs while still warm: Warm egg whites bond securely to inner shells. Always plunge into ice water for at least 15 minutes before peeling.

source.name: 10 Mistakes Everyone Makes Cooking Eggs - Food Network
source.location: Mistake 7: Peeling Hard-Cooked Eggs While They're Hot

methods.doneness: Soft, creamy curds that are just set and still slightly glossy
methods.rest: 1 minute on warm plate (carryover heat finishes cooking)
methods.tips: Preheat pan with a thin layer of melted butter; keep heat gentle and stir with a heat-resistant spatula, removing pan from heat while curds are still slightly soft.

source.name: 10 Mistakes Everyone Makes Cooking Eggs - Food Network

methods.cut: whole cracked eggs (sunny-side up or over-easy)
methods.heat: Medium heat (or medium-high oil briefly, then immediately reduced to low)
methods.time: 2 to 3 minutes for sunny-side up; flip and cook 30–45 seconds for over-easy
methods.doneness: Whites completely opaque and set; yolk warm and runny
methods.tips: Crack egg onto a flat counter first; slide into preheated greased skillet and lower heat immediately so whites remain tender.

source.name: 10 Mistakes Everyone Makes Cooking Eggs - Food Network
source.location: Mistake 4: Cooking Eggs Over High Heat

methods.time: 6 to 7 minutes for soft-boiled; 9 to 11 minutes for hard-boiled
methods.doneness: Hard-boiled: yolk completely set with no gray ring; soft-boiled: firm white with warm jammy yolk
methods.rest: Soak in an ice water bath for at least 15 minutes before peeling
methods.tips: Never allow water to violently boil; plunge directly into an ice water bath immediately after timing to ease shell removal.

source.name: 10 Mistakes Everyone Makes Cooking Eggs - Food Network

methods.doneness: 160°F internal temperature; puffed, golden top with center fully set
methods.tips: Thoroughly grease baking dish; combine whole eggs with milk/cream and cheeses for structure that stays moist without weeping.
